question.text: Ankit, aged 35, has the following health insurance payments in FY 2024-25: Rs.28,000 for self and family, Rs.55,000 for his parents (both aged 62 and 64), and Rs.5,000 for preventive health check-up for himself. Under Section 80D, what is the maximum deduction he can claim under the old regime?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 80D in the old regime: (a) Self and family (non-senior): maximum Rs.25,000. Ankit paid Rs.28,000, but the cap restricts the deduction to Rs.25,000, and the Rs.5,000 preventive health check-up is subsumed within (not added on top of) this cap. (b) Parents who are senior citizens: maximum Rs.50,000. He paid Rs.55,000, but the cap limits this leg to Rs.50,000. Total deduction = Rs.25,000 + Rs.50,000 = Rs.75,000. (Section 80D is unavailable under the new tax regime.) The Trap: Rs.88,000 simply totals all payments without applying any cap. Rs.80,000 incorrectly treats the Rs.5,000 preventive check-up as additional to the Rs.25,000 self/family cap. Rs.50,000 ignores the self/family leg entirely. Note: Cross-Exam Context paragraph removed and the role-specific pro-tip label replaced with a neutral Exam Tip framing for the investment-adviser audience.
